correctness.rationale: The incomplete-beta terms are exactly binomial tail probabilities, so the copula equals \(n^{-1}E[\min(J_u,J_v)]\). Off the diagonal, stochastic monotonicity pushes the defect to the diagonal. On the diagonal, the defect is \(E|J-K|/(2n)\). A lazy-walk representation shows this is maximized at \(p=1/2\), and the resulting centered \(\operatorname{Bin}(2n,1/2)\) absolute deviation telescopes exactly to \(n\binom{2n}{n}/4^n\). All quantifiers and the parameter shift \(n=m+1\) are explicit. The verifier checks only identities already proved analytically.

value.rationale: The direct source singles out the EPD Bernstein construction as an extremal positive-dependence point and explicitly presents exchangeable Bernstein analysis as a natural next direction. Baker's earlier work shows that the same family approaches the Fréchet bound but gives only qualitative convergence. The exact worst-case uniform defect, its center location, and its sharp \(n^{-1/2}\) constant quantify a natural global approximation property of this canonical family rather than an arbitrary parameter slice.
